# config/ — configuration

Design principle: **a small number of model bases + command-line deltas + batches driven by
loops** — not one yaml per experiment.

Reproduction does not depend on any yaml file: `results/pretrain/**/run_meta.json` stores the
complete effective config snapshot *after* overrides are applied (`config_path` records the
base, the snapshot records the truth).

## Layout

```
config/
├── base/                  # 6 model bases: beatmae / himae / mmr / xmae / papagei / probe
├── campaign_example.yaml  # campaign orchestration template (consumed by eval/run_campaign.py)
├── campaign_full.yaml     # the concrete downstream campaign config used for this paper
└── README.md
```

How bases map to `models/`: `beatmae` → `train/pretrain.py`; `himae`/`mmr`/`xmae` →
`train/pretrain_baseline.py`; `papagei` → `train/pretrain_papagei.py`; `probe` → the
downstream probe heads.

**A different entry point does not mean a different family**: PaPaGei has no masking and no
patchification and therefore gets its own entry point, but it belongs to the same comparison
axis.

### Auxiliary-task statistics (`feat_stats*.npz`)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `config/feat_stats_v2c.npz` | Referenced directly by `config/base/beatmae.yaml` under `feat_stats:`; `train/pretrain.py` uses it for the auxiliary task's z-parameterization |

To rebuild the current one by hand:

```bash
python preprocess/corpus_build/compute_feat_stats.py <corpus_v2c> config/feat_stats_v2c.npz
```

Statistics are computed from 2000 segments drawn corpus-wide with `np.random.default_rng(0)`,
so the result is reproducible. Note that the script's **built-in default corpus root is
`corpus_v2`** — you must pass the `corpus_v2c` root explicitly.

## Base contents = model invariants

A base contains only architecture and protocol defaults (model dimensions, masking mode,
training hyperparameters). The following fields have **no default in the base** and **must be
overridden on the command line**:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `out_dir` | Output directory for the run; points directly into the four-level weight tree `results/pretrain/<family>/<corpus>/<variant>` |
| `data.sources` | Training source combination: `null` = all sources / `[mimic]` single source / `[mimic,vital,aurora]` = 3src |
| `corpus_root` (if not on the default machine) | The built-in default will not match your machine — override it with your own corpus path |

## Usage

Single experiment:

```bash
python train/pretrain_baseline.py config/base/himae.yaml \
    data.sources=[aurora] out_dir=results/pretrain/himae/v2c_aurora/mr065_sqrt
```

The last three segments of `out_dir` are `<family>/<corpus>/<variant>` and must line up with an
existing slot in the weight tree:

- **family** = model generation —
  `legacy_v2_all` / `v2c_3src_mva` / `v2c_4src_mvaiwb` / `v2c_iwb` / `v2c_aurora` …
- **variant** = mask ratio × sampling mode, e.g. `mr065_sqrt` / `anchor_mr065_traverse`

The `run_dir` column of the local experiment ledger (regenerated by the ledger scripts, which
are not part of the release) lists the existing slots for any family/corpus.

Batch (one shell script = one campaign; loop and queue):

```bash
for src in mimic vital aurora; do
  for m in himae mmr xmae; do
    nohup python train/pretrain_baseline.py config/base/$m.yaml \
      data.sources=[$src] out_dir=results/pretrain/${m}/v2c_${src}/mr065_sqrt \
      >> results/logs/bl_matrix.log 2>&1 &
  done
done
```

(Confirm your slot names before launching a new combination.)

Ratio/sampling ablation deltas work the same way: `baseline.mask_ratio=0.5`,
`train.sampler_mode=traverse`.

## ⚠ `out_dir` is not validated — reruns overwrite

Both pretraining entry points currently do `mkdir(..., exist_ok=True)` and write
`ckpt/best.pt` once the target is reached. **If the target directory already exists and
contains a `ckpt/best.pt`, it will be silently overwritten.** Before rerunning an experiment
with the same name, change `out_dir`. (`--resume` exists and is the intended path for
continuing an interrupted run.)

## Campaign layer (downstream probe orchestration)

One yaml = one complete campaign: **an experiment list × the stages to run**, consumed by
`eval/run_campaign.py`. Note the order of magnitude — the number of configs equals the number
of campaigns (single digits), not the number of experiments (dozens).

```bash
python eval/run_campaign.py config/campaign_example.yaml --dry-run        # print the commands only
python eval/run_campaign.py config/campaign_example.yaml                  # run everything
python eval/run_campaign.py config/campaign_example.yaml --only myexp     # a subset
python eval/run_campaign.py config/campaign_example.yaml --tasks extract,stream
python eval/run_campaign.py config/campaign_example.yaml --corpus /path   # override the corpus root
```

Stage order is fixed: `extract` (`scripts/extract_embeddings.py`) → `stream`
(`scripts/materialize_stream.py` to materialize, then `scripts/probe_full_stream.py`, per
experiment). The `window` stage has been retired; writing `window` in a yaml raises an explicit
error rather than being silently skipped.

CLI deltas take precedence over yaml. Embedding caches (large intermediates) stay under
`results/cache/embeddings/`.

## When a new yaml is justified

Only for **long-list configs** (experiment lists, campaign definitions) that do not fit on a
command line. Write `config/campaign_<name>.yaml` — one file per campaign, never one per
experiment. For reproduction, the `run_meta.json` snapshot is authoritative.
